output.description: The recipe Handle and every unit it trains.

warnings.description: Caveats on this result, most actionable first. Empty when there are none.

fields.description: Always exactly `code`, `message`, `columns`, `param`, `hint`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: A caveat on a successful result: it worked, but read this first. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `code`: The warning's Error Code. Branch on this, not on ``message``.
Position 1, `message`: What happened and what to do, in one or two sentences.
Position 2, `columns`: Columns the warning concerns, or null.
Position 3, `param`: The argument the warning concerns, or null.

omitted.description: One entry per list that was cut, naming the Operation that returns the rest. Empty when nothing was cut.

fields.description: Always exactly `field`, `shown`, `total`, `operation`, `reason`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: Something left out of a result: a capped list was cut, or a Literal Field withheld. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `field`: Name of the list field that was cut, or the path of the Literal Field withheld, such as ``top_values[].value``.
Position 1, `shown`: How many items the list holds; 0 for a withheld Literal Field.
Position 2, `total`: How many items exist; for a withheld Literal Field, how many values at that path are null.
Position 3, `operation`: The Operation that returns the rest, or null when no Operation does.
Position 4, `reason`: ``cap`` when a list was cut to its cap; ``literal_policy`` when the Operator's Literal Policy is ``deny``.

recipe.description: Recipe Handle, such as ``recipe_7f3a9c2e``. It holds its own copy of the routing.

profile.description: The profile Handle the routing was made from.

units.description: Every unit, in routing order: a joint block where its first column sits in the dataset. Empty when no column fills values. At most 100; past 100, ``omitted`` counts the rest and names ``explain_routing``, whose columns give each one's id as ``<strategy>:<column>``.

fields.description: Always exactly `unit_id`, `strategy`, `columns`, in this order. A row's value at position i is the field named here at i.

rows.description: One unit of work ``fit_unit`` trains: a joint block or one column. One row per record, its values in `fields` order. The i-th schema below describes position i.

anyOf.description: Position 0, `unit_id`: The unit id ``fit_unit`` takes: ``mice`` or ``knn`` for a joint block, ``<strategy>:<column>`` for one column, such as ``median:age``.
Position 1, `strategy`: The strategy the unit trains.

Position 2, `columns`: The columns the unit fills, in dataset order: every column of a joint block, or its one column. At most 100; past 100, ``omitted`` counts the rest and names ``explain_routing``.
